figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 1.
Cyclization of geranylgeranyl diphosphate to taxa-4(5),11(12)-diene and elaboration of the oleﬁn intermediate to Taxol.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 2.
Conversion of isopentenyl diphosphate (IPP) to dimethylallyl diphosphate (DMAPP) by isopentenyl diphosphate isomerase (A) and
the geranylgeranyl diphosphate (GGPP) synthase-catalyzed condensation of IPP with the allylic diphosphate cosubstrates DMAPP, geranyl
diphosphate (GPP), and farnesyl diphosphate (FPP) (B). Product chain length and double bond geometry are determined by the speciﬁcity
of the prenyltransferase. The solvolysis products geranylgeraniol (GGOH), geranyllinalool (GLOH), and geranylnerol (GNOH) derived by
treatment of GGPP with methanolic HCl are also illustrated (C).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 3.
The nucleotide coding sequence and deduced amino acid sequence of T. canadensis GGPP synthase. The arrowheads indicate
positions at which the sequence was truncated at the 59-terminus to remove the presumptive transit peptide.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 4.
Amino acid sequence comparison of eight GGPP synthases of plant origin. The thin underline indicates the region corresponding
to the putative transit peptide. The heavily underlined regions designated I and II are regions that contain highly conserved Asp and Arg
residues that have been shown to be important in catalysis (53–56). The residues boxed in black indicate positional identity, while similar
amino acids are indicated by gray shading. The species from which the GGPP synthases were obtained are indicated in the left column.
Species abbreviations and Genbank Accession Nos. are: Arth, Arabidopsis thaliana, Z99708; Arth2, A. thaliana sequence 2, D85029 (58);
Arth3, A. thaliana sequence 3, L40577 (71); Caan, Capsicum annuum, X80267, (24); Caro, Catharanthus roseus, X92893 (72); Lual, Lupinus
albus, U15778 (73); Sial, Sinapis alba, X98795 (31); and Taca, Taxus canadensis (this work, AF081514).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 5.
Relationship of eight plant-derived GGPP synthase se-
quences based on amino acid similarity. The species abbreviations
are the same as those described in the legend to Fig. 4.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 6.
Complementation of a bet2-1 mutation in S. cerevisiae
ANY119 by T. canadensis GGPP synthase grown on SGI (glucose
containing) medium. From bottom clockwise on each plate: control
(empty vector), full length (preprotein), Tr295 (F99 truncation), and
Tr313 (M105 truncation). The plate on the left was incubated at 25°C
(permissive temperature) while the one on the right was incubated at
37°C (restrictive temperature).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 7.
Toxicity of T. canadensis full-length preprotein and trun-
cated Tr295 GGPP synthase constructs in S. cerevisiae INVSc1
grown on SLI (galactose containing) medium. The plating pattern is
the same as that described in the legend to Fig. 6.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 8
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 8.
Silver-stained SDS–PAGE (2.1 mg of crude protein per
lane) prepared from INVSc1 cells transformed with pYeDP60 con-
structs of GGPP synthase. The lanes are control (empty vector) (1),
full-length construct (preprotein) (2), Tr295 (F99 truncation) (3),
Tr313 (M105 truncation) (4), and the 31.2 kDa marker, carbonic
anhydrase (5).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 9
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 9.
Radio-GC analysis of the reaction product generated by T. canadensis GGPP synthase construct Tr295 followed by acid-catalyzed
solvolysis. The smooth lower tracing indicates the elution pattern of the authentic standards geranyllinalool (mixed isomers, the all-trans-
isomer elutes at 20.93 min) and geranylgeraniol (Rt 5 27.68 min). The radioactive component with Rt 5 25.93 min is consistent with the
elution behavior of geranylnerol.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 10
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 10.
Northern analysis of mRNA levels for GGPP synthase and taxadiene synthase after methyl jasmonate induction. The time the
cells were harvested after methyl jasmonate induction is indicated above each lane. The total RNA loaded per lane was 14.5 mg. The 3.8- and
1.9-kb transcripts corresponding to taxadiene synthase and GGPP synthase, respectively, are illustrated (A), as is the ethidium bromide
stained control gel showing the 18 S and 28 S rRNAs (B).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 11
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 11.
Time course of GGPP synthase (Œ) and taxadiene synthase (F) activity measured in extracts of T. canadensis suspension cell
cultures following induction with methyl jasmonate. The 0-h time point corresponds to the enzyme activities from cells harvested
immediately prior to methyl jasmonate addition. For details of the isolation and assays, see Experimental Procedures.
